text: Kissing Students (Estonian: Suudlevad tudengid) is a sculpture and fountain situated in Raekoja plats, Tartu, Estonia, located in front of Tartu Town Hall. It is one of the most recognizable symbols of the city, reflecting Tartu's status as Estonia's "intellectual capital" and "student capital," a reputation rooted in the city's home to the nation's oldest and most prestigious university, the University of Tartu.[1][2][3] The fountain was constructed in 1948 and was especially favored by newlyweds, who believed standing there would bring good fortune for their future.[1] The sculpture was designed in 1998 by Mati Karmin.[1] Its geographical coordinates are 58°22′49″N 26°43′23″E﻿ / ﻿58.38021°N 26.72296°E﻿ / 58.38021; 26.72296.
